change.title: pr-10
change.description: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Migration crashes when there is no `embed_category` row in site_settings
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` indexes the first row of the result without checking that a row exists. `embed_category` defaults to `''` (see the removed entry in config/site_settings.yml), and default values are not stored in `site_settings`. On any site that never set it, or set it to a name that no longer matches a category, the join returns zero rows. `[0]` then raises (an IndexError on an empty `PG::Result`, never a nil that falls through to the `category_id == 0` fallback on line 14), and the whole migration aborts. Check `cmd_tuples > 0` before indexing, as you already do for `embeddable_hosts` on line 19. The same applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw and may never match
findings.body: Each line of the old setting is inserted as-is. The old `allows_embeddable_host?` accepted `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234` entries (see the removed specs and the old embed_controller_spec). The new model strips scheme and path in `before_validation` and compares `lower(host) = <referer host>` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`. A migrated row such as `http://discourse.org` is stored with its scheme, so it never matches and embedding silently stops working for that site. Other problems with the same line: lines are not stripped, so a `\r` or blank line becomes a row (blank lines become empty hosts); values are not lowercased; and `'#{h}'` is interpolated without quoting, so a `'` in the setting breaks the SQL. Normalize each value with the same rules as the model (strip scheme and path, strip whitespace, downcase, skip blanks) and quote it with `connection.quote`.

findings.title: Irreversible migration inside `change`; old settings deleted with no `down`
findings.body: The raw `execute` statements (the INSERTs and the DELETE of `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category`) inside `change` are not reversible. Rolling back raises IrreversibleMigration, and the old setting values are gone once this runs. `create_table ... force: true` also drops an existing `embeddable_hosts` table. Use explicit `up`/`down`, with `down` restoring the settings from the table, or at least make it clear that the migration is one-way.

findings.title: After saving without choosing a category, the row shows an empty category
findings.body: A new host starts with `categoryId` null. The server then assigns `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25) and returns it as `category_id`. The component ignores that and does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` with the null id, so `category-badge host.category` renders nothing until the page is reloaded. The admin sees a blank category while the real one is Uncategorized. Use the id the server returned, for example `host.get('category_id')` after the save, instead of the local `categoryId`.

findings.title: Delete failure is silent
findings.body: `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save`. If the DELETE fails (for example a 404 or 500), the admin gets no message and the row stays. Add the same error handler.

findings.title: Missing record or missing params give a 500 instead of 404 or a validation error
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id. `save_host(nil)` (line 11) then raises NoMethodError on `host.host=`, and `host.destroy` (line 16) raises too. Use `find`, which gives a 404. `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` (line 23) also raises if the nested hash is absent. Related: `category_id` is not checked to be an existing category, and the table has no FK, so a bogus id or a later deleted category leaves a host whose `category` is nil. In `TopicEmbed.import` that falls back silently to the default category.

findings.title: `before_validation` raises on a nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called on a nil `host`, which raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation. `sub!` also mutates the string in place, so it modifies the caller's (params) string. Guard with `host.present?` or assign a new value: `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

findings.title: Validation accepts hosts that the matcher can never match (ports, case)
findings.body: The format validation on line 2 allows `example.com:8080`, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI(host).host`, which excludes the port. A saved `example.com:8080` row therefore never matches, with no error shown to the admin. The comparison is `lower(host) = ?` but the right-hand side is not downcased, and Ruby's `URI#host` does not normalize case. A referer like `http://Example.com/..` is rejected even though the row is stored as `example.com`. Either drop the port from the accepted format or compare `host:port`, and call `host.downcase` before the query.

findings.title: No uniqueness on host
findings.body: Duplicate hosts can be created (UI, API or migration). `record_for_host` then returns an arbitrary `.first` with no ordering, so which category embedded topics land in is nondeterministic. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and ideally a unique index in the migration.

findings.title: `saveChanges` and the server `update` action are dead and do nothing
findings.body: No template references `saveChanges`. `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (embedding_controller.rb:9) only re-renders the OpenStruct and persists nothing, and the PUT route in config/routes.rb:139 exists only for it. Remove the action, the route and the `update` method until there is something to save.

findings.title: `_ids` hydration changes a shared code path; failed lookups are kept as undefined
findings.body: The regex now matches every key ending in `_ids` on any rest-serialized payload, and calls `obj[k].map` unconditionally, so a null or non-array value throws. `map` always returns an array, so `hydrated || []` on line 200 is dead. Ids that `_lookupSubType` can't resolve become `undefined` entries in the resulting list instead of being skipped. Unlike the singular branch, the `_ids` key is deleted even when nothing resolved. Filter out undefined results and guard for a non-array. Separately, `type.replace('_', '-')` in adapters/rest.js.es6:22 replaces only the first underscore and is a no-op for hyphenated types, which is all the new code passes.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `:embeddable_host`, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category`. Fabrication loads every file so the specs still work, but anyone looking for a fabricator by file name will look in the wrong file. Put each definition in the file that matches its name.

findings.title: Test name no longer matches what it tests, and the behavior change is not covered
findings.body: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer exercises any embeddable host, because `expandable_first_post?` no longer reads hosts (topic.rb:869). It passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is not stubbed. The method now returns true on `embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` regardless of hosts, so a topic embedded from a host that was later removed still gets an expandable first post. Rename or remove the test, and decide whether the host check should be kept. The `describe 'with an emeddable host'` label has a typo, and its host fabrication is now irrelevant to the assertions.

findings.title: Admin controller specs only assert the superclass
findings.body: Both new controller specs only check `< Admin::AdminController`. Nothing covers create, update or destroy of hosts, the serializer shape, non-staff access, or the data migration, which is the riskiest part of this change. `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` has no cases for invalid hosts, nil host, ports or case, and its describe block is still named "allows_embeddable_host".

contracts.action: Data migration moves the embeddable_hosts and embed_category settings into the new table, then deletes the settings
contracts.equivalent_path: Old SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts / embed_category read by SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? and TopicEmbed.import
contracts.before_after: Before: the allow-list was a newline-separated setting that accepted scheme-prefixed entries. After: rows are copied verbatim, with no normalization, and the settings are deleted.
contracts.visible_effect: Hosts stored with http(s):// or a path never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, so embedding is silently denied after upgrade. Sites with no embed_category row fail the migration.
contracts.failure_mode: Insert and delete run in one migration. If an INSERT raises (quote in host), the migration aborts and nothing is deleted. The `[0]['id']` lookup raises on empty results. Raw execute inside `change` cannot be rolled back.

contracts.action: Destructive: `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts','embed_category')`; and `host.destroy` in the admin controller
contracts.before_after: The migration deletes by fixed setting names, inside the same migration transaction as the inserts. The controller deletes one row by params[:id] and removes only that row. Neither re-verifies the target, but each is scoped to a single name or id.
contracts.visible_effect: Old settings are gone after migrating, and the migrated hosts must be correct because they cannot be re-derived. A DELETE for an unknown id gives a 500.
contracts.failure_mode: destroy on nil raises NoMethodError, so the admin sees a generic error. If the migrated rows are wrong (scheme-prefixed hosts), the original values are lost.

contracts.action: Admin saves a host from the embedding screen (new or edit)
contracts.equivalent_path: RestModel.save, _saveNew or update, via the REST adapter with ADMIN_MODELS (/admin/embeddable_hosts)
contracts.before_after: Same generic REST path used by plugin and site-customization. The create response is merged with setProperties without hydration, so `category_id` is set but `category` is not.
contracts.visible_effect: The row leaves edit mode and shows host plus category badge. With no category chosen, the badge is blank even though the server stored Uncategorized.
contracts.failure_mode: Rejection goes to popupAjaxError and the row stays in edit mode, which is visible. A validation failure returns render_json_error, and `isSaving` is cleared in finally.

contracts.action: Embed access check now reads the embeddable_hosts table (ensure_embeddable, TopicRetriever.invalid_host?, TopicEmbed.import category)
contracts.before_after: Before: the controller raised if the setting was blank, then checked the referer host against the setting. After: only the table lookup remains. An empty table means record_for_host returns nil and the request is denied, so the guard is not needed.
contracts.visible_effect: Referers not matching a stored host get InvalidAccess. Topics created through import land in the host's category.
contracts.failure_mode: Unparseable referer gives URI error, rescued to nil, so it is denied (fail closed). The dev-admin bypass at line 60 is unchanged.

contracts.action: New admin Embedding screen loads via store.find('embedding') and hydrates embeddable_host_ids
contracts.equivalent_path: Other rest-serialized finds through the store, now with the added `_ids` branch in _hydrateEmbedded
contracts.before_after: The embedding adapter overrides pathFor to a fixed URL. The server returns an OpenStruct 'default' with hosts as sideloaded ids, and the store turns them into an `embeddable_hosts` array.
contracts.visible_effect: Table of hosts appears. Hosts added in the UI are pushed onto that array, and new rows are removed from it again on cancel.
contracts.failure_mode: If the GET rejects, the route's model hook fails and the standard Ember error route is shown. The list is loaded once per route entry, so Back remounts re-fetch the model, but the store identity map persists. A saved host's `category` comes from the local categoryId and not the payload.

summary: The change replaces the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with an EmbeddableHost table and an admin UI. The main problem is the data migration. It raises on sites with no `embed_category` row, and it copies scheme-prefixed hosts verbatim, so they never match the new lookup. It is also irreversible. Secondary problems: the model accepts hosts the matcher can never match (ports, case), the new admin controller returns 500 for a missing record or missing params, a new host saved without a category shows a blank category until reload, and the fabricator files have swapped contents. The tests are thin or mis-named, and the new `_ids` hydration in the store applies to every rest-serialized payload. I read the repository's code only and did not run anything.
